chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Substituting for the Marine Band on WEAF radio
summary: Walking in unannounced, his band is put on air to replace the Marine Band and succeeds.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I can play the blues. But I don't want you to hold me to it. I want to play what I want to play. What I think is good and not but -- I'm not Perry Bradford, and I'm not Mamie Smith. I'll do what I want to do. If you want me you want me. The same as Paul Specht or Paul Whiteman would do. And I had good arrangements, because I had good numbers. We did in the Club Alabam -- no, I'm sorry, it was the Nest. We -- seven, eight men made a substitution for the Marine Band in Washington, for one hour over WEAF. We'd come down there to see about getting a broadcast. And just when we were there, that night, it was around 4 o'clock in the afternoon or 3 o'clock in the afternoon. We just picked up our horns and went down there. And went walking into the studio. And the man said, "What do you want?" We said, "We'd like to do a radio program." And he looked at us and he said, "Well, I don't know, I don't know what we have." And that time, it was just our luck. It was time, it looked like it was time for us. The phone rang and something happened and the Marine Band was supposed to come on at eight o'clock for an hour. And they couldn't do it for some reason. So he come to me and said, "Would you like to sub-
stitute for the Marine Band in Washington?" And I said, "Are you kidding", "do you know who we are?"

With eight men, the Marine Band? Was one of the best bands in America, then see? And I said, "No, I don't think so." And he said, "Well, you might be able to do it by changing the style of music." See, they gonna play marches and you all play jazz, you see? And so he said, I said, "Alright, I'll try it." And he said, "Well, let me see what you can do." We played, "Where the Ganges Flows". This was on the style of Paul Whiteman, though.

(sings) And we -- it was an arrangement see, that they had never heard before. So whether it was good or bad, it was something they had never heard before. The man said, "You don't have to finish it. You're good." Have you got another number?" Said, "Yeah, got a whole book of numbers like that." Which we did. So he said, "Well, I'll tell you, you guys go home and clean up and shine your shoes and shine your horns up and be down here at half past seven and we'll put you on." We come back at half past seven, in fact we didn't go uptown, I was afraid to let the guys go uptown. So we sat down in the Horn and Hardart and did our planning and had something to eat and stayed right downtown until right after the broadcast. We didn't have to go

to work til nine thirty or ten o'clock, see. So, we made it and we was a success, see? We substituted for the Marine Band, and if somebody had of told me that I was going to do that, I would have said, 'Are you crazy?' But it shows you, when you're young and you're dedicated, you try things that you wouldn't dare. Like Little David tried with Goliath. Well, what other fool would go out there with a slingshot to kill a man as big as Goliath. That's what we did. That's exactly what we did.
